correctness.rationale: The normalization has genus 5 while an irreducible plane sextic has arithmetic genus 10, so the total delta defect is 5. The source proves that the central point is a node and that a three-singularity model has one symmetric pair of further multiplicity-two points; each member therefore has delta 2. In Case III the source's formal split form plus transverse evenness forces exponent 4, hence A3. In Case II the source's second coefficient system is exactly a triple-root condition and would force A2, contradicting delta 2; the surviving double-root system, evenness, and delta 2 force A3. A replayable symbolic/example checker independently verifies the algebraic identities used in these reductions.

value.rationale: The nongeneric three-point models are a natural boundary stratum in the source's complete singularity classification. Determining their exact ADE basket replaces an unspecified higher-contact double point by the precise tacnode type and shows that one branch of the source's coefficient criterion is geometrically spurious on the Howe locus. This is structurally useful for resolution, function-field, and degeneration calculations and is not an arbitrary parameter slice.
